children: The benchmark indices fell more than 1.6 percent on September 24, with weakness in market breadth. About 2,476 shares declined, compared with 772 shares that advanced on the NSE. Given the prevailing caution, the market may see further consolidation, while any recovery is likely to attract selling pressure. Here are some short-term trading ideas to consider:
Jay Mehta, Technical Research at JM Financial Services

Inventurus Knowledge Solutions has given a breakout above a sloping channel in which it had been trading for more than two months. Price is currently trading above its short-term and long-term moving averages.
The recent breakout was supported by strong positive volume. Trend and momentum indicators remain in bullish territory and support continued upside. Overall trend stays positive.

HBL Engineering has broken out of a consolidation range and trendline and is currently trading above its short-term, medium-term, and long-term moving averages. Momentum and trend indicators support a bullish outlook. The recent breakout was accompanied by strong volume participation, indicating positive accumulation and healthy buyer interest.

Alembic Pharma has broken out above a tight consolidation range as well as a sloping trendline. The stock is currently hovering near the breakout retest zone. Recent sessions have witnessed strong volume participation, indicating ongoing accumulation.

Price is trading above short-term, medium-term, and long-term moving averages, which should provide support on any minor dips. Volumes have been consistently building above the 20-day average, reflecting robust participation. Momentum and trend indicators continue to support a bullish bias.
Om Mehra, Technical Research Analyst at Samco Securities

Arvind broke out of its Rs 540–550 consolidation zone with a decisive move higher, underscored by identical open and low. The stock surged on higher volumes, running well above the recent average and reflecting strong participation. The Supertrend remains in bullish mode and is placed as a major support, providing a cushion to the downside.

The RSI is placed near 56 and has turned higher from the lower end of its recent range, indicating improving momentum. A sustained close above the Rs 570 zone would further strengthen the near-term setup.
Hence, one can consider long positions at the CMP of Rs 565.70, with an expected move toward Rs 600 and a stop-loss at Rs 548.

RR Kabel has witnessed a sharp correction and has been forming a rounding bottom pattern near the Rs 2,350–2,400 zone over the past few weeks. The stock is now recovering steadily from that base and is approaching the 20-day SMA, which remains the immediate level to watch for a decisive reclaim.

The open and low nearly coincide, reflecting the strength of the daily candle. The RSI has recovered sharply from deeply oversold levels with a positive divergence. Hence, one can consider long positions at the CMP of Rs 2,529.8, with an expected move toward Rs 2,700 and a stop-loss at Rs 2,430.

SKF India has been respecting the rising trendline on the daily chart, building a base in the Rs 1,480-1,510 zone and gradually recovering. The stock is now consolidating just above the VWAP (volume weighted average price) placed at Rs 1,530 and is trading above the Supertrend placed at Rs 1,475, which continues to provide a reliable cushion on declines. The stock has regained position above the 20- and 50-day SMAs.

The RSI has recovered to the 50 mark after spending a period in the lower zone. A sustained close above Rs 1,555 would improve the near-term outlook meaningfully. Hence, one can consider long positions at the CMP of Rs 1,542, with an expected move toward Rs 1,640 and a stop-loss at Rs 1,495.
